reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Bacterial Conjunctivitis Pink Eye: thick yellow-green purulent discharge gluing eyelids shut in the morning with diffuse redness without vision loss. 25F presenting with bilateral conjunctival injection, gritty sensation, and copious purulent discharge crusting lashes closed where vision and pupils are normal responding to topical Polymyxin B-Trimethoprim eye drops.
reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Bacterial Conjunctivitis Pink Eye.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Bacterial Conjunctivitis Pink Eye.
reference_soap.plan: Assess visual acuity and exclude corneal involvement. Provide hand hygiene and avoid sharing towels or eye cosmetics. Uncomplicated bacterial conjunctivitis may resolve without antibiotics; topical polymyxin B-trimethoprim is a reasonable treatment option when clinically indicated. Urgently assess for contact-lens-associated keratitis or other ocular disease if there is pain, photophobia, reduced vision, or corneal opacity.

exam.finding: Alert, comfortable-appearing young woman with bilateral conjunctival hyperemia and dried yellowish crust along the eyelid margins.
Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.8°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.

Visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes, pupils are equal and reactive to light without afferent pupillary defect, extraocular movements are full without pain, and fluorescein staining shows clear corneas without epithelial defects.
Diffuse bilateral conjunctival injection with copious thick yellowish-green purulent discharge; upper eyelid eversion reveals no foreign bodies, follicles, or subconjunctival hemorrhage.
No palpable preauricular, submandibular, or anterior cervical lymph nodes.
